I remember reading somewhere on these forums that for some reason, not everyone is getting a tracking number e-mail.  That's fine and I accept that on a shipment of this scale, everything can't be done right away, but that hasn't stopped my anxiety issues from screaming "YOU DID SOMETHING WRONG AND YOU'LL NEVER GET YOUR THING AND IT'S ALL YOUR FAULT!"  Stupid anxiety.  I'm thrilled about this game, doubly so because it's arriving four months early, but now I'm worried that I'll worry myself into an ulcer, which makes me worry more because I don't have health insurance and can't afford any medical bills.

Stupid anxiety.  Stupid brain.

I apologize for the rant.

I also never received any email with a tracking number, but I was able to locate a tracking number through fedex.com and eventually track mine. I also live in California and mine is expected to arrive on Thursday! So you just may be amazed too. Anyway, below I've written how I was able to track down tracking info. Not sure if it'll work for you, but hopefully if it does, it can ease some of your worries.

From my Kickstarter post:

"Try this. It took me less than five minutes.

Go to fedex.com … find the set of links under "Quick Access" … click "Customize Your Delivery" … this will take you to a page about FedEx Delivery Manager. Then you can sign up for an account, by providing name, address, etc. (no credit card info needed). This will allow you to set it up to be notified of future deliveries going to your address.

However, since the shipments have already gone out, you likely won't get an email with a tracking number (I didn't). You will just get the email confirmations about signing up for fedex.com and FedEx Delivery Manager. But, if you go back to the website, click on Customize Your Delivery, then login w/ your new account information, it should take you to a page where you can see any pending deliveries, get the tracking number, etc.

At least this worked for me. I can't guarantee it will work for everyone… "

Good luck!

posts.name: chainsawrabbit
posts.cooked:
Got my package of Sentinel Tactics awesomeness last Thursday, and haven't really stopped playing it yet.  Getting a lot of skirmishes in, trying out all the characters and getting a solid feel for range probabilities, line of sight, and movement.  The only reason it gets put away at night is so the kitten won't decide it's a playground in the middle of the night and I have to spend half of every morning finding the pieces.

My copy was, thankfully, 100% complete.  The only hang-up was that some of the miniatures didn't quite fit onto their bases (mainly The Wraith, Swift Bot, and a few Citizens), or some wouldn't hold on to the base at all without glue (all the single-peg figures).  Gave me an excuse to pick up a file set and some model glue, which will come in handy in a few months since I Kickstarted an extremely miniatures-heavy game that should be arriving soon.

I considered leaving them off the bases in case I ever get them painted, but reality won out: I have no skill at painting miniatures, I sure as Hell don't want to use these to practice on, and I'll never be able to afford to pay someone to paint them.  They'll just have to look monochromatically awesome, which they do.
